section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/python/ruff.toml.tmpl:1-18` (no `target-version`) | Ruff runs with `--config .gspot/config/ruff.toml`, and that file sets no `target-version`. So Ruff ignores the project's `requires-python`. In a sample with `requires-python = ">=3.8"`, Ruff offered UP045 (`X \| None`) and UP006 (`list[int]`) as automatic fixes. `gspot check --fix` applies them, and the code then fails on Python 3.8 and 3.9. When `ruff.toml` sits next to `pyproject.toml`, Ruff reports FA100 instead. | Write `target-version` from the scope's `requires-python`. `packages/cli/src/repository/packages.ts:123` already reads it. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/python/manifest.toml:85-88` (`[[config]]` ruff, no `pointer`) | Init removes `ruff.toml`, `.ruff.toml`, and `[tool.ruff]` (lines 27-36), and the kit writes no root pointer for Ruff. So the Ruff in a developer's editor uses its defaults: line length 88 instead of gspot's 120, and a different rule set. Format on save and `python/ruff-format` then keep rewriting the same lines. | Write a root `ruff.toml` pointer that holds `extend = ".gspot/config/ruff.toml"`. The basedpyright pointer already uses `extends` this way. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/python/basedpyrightconfig.json.tmpl:2-108` (no `venvPath`, `venv`) | The configuration names no interpreter. gspot runs basedpyright from `.gspot/.venv` (`packages/cli/src/tools/locate.ts:26`) and sets no `VIRTUAL_ENV`. In a sample, a package installed in the project's `.venv` gave `reportMissingImports`, which is an error at both levels. Adding `venvPath` and `venv` cleared it. In a hook or CI shell with no active environment, every third-party import fails `python/basedpyright`. | When the scope has a `.venv`, write `"venvPath"` and `"venv"`. Add a setting for projects that keep the interpreter somewhere else. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/python/manifest.toml:142-154` (import-linter), `:171-184` (deptry) | Both run from gspot's environment, so they cannot see the project's installed packages. Both reported `cd "$dir"`, and gspot also reported `cd "$dir" && ls`, which is safe. `recursive-remove` reports every `rm -rf` outside `tools.bash.safety_owners`, which defaults to an empty list. That includes the `trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT` line that `bash/contract` requires after `mktemp` (`packages/cli/src/checks/language/bash/contract.ts:159-162`). `\|\| true` is the usual way to allow a failure under `set -e`, which `contract` also requires. | Remove `unchecked-cd`, and let ShellCheck own it. Exempt `rm` inside a trap for a `mktemp` path. Move `blanket-success` to `all`, or delete it. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/src/config/checks/language/bash.ts:147,159-162` (used by `bash/safety`) | These patterns come from one project's cleanup scripts. One reports sourcing a file whose name holds `state`, `snapshot`, or `last_config`. Others report clearing `${HOME}/.cache`, `/root/.cache`, and `/dev/shm/*`. | Delete them. ShellCheck SC2115 already covers `rm -rf "$var/"` when `$var` is empty. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/bash/manifest.toml:133-134` (shfmt `-i {indent}`) | `{indent}` is `format.indent_width` (`packages/cli/src/execution/tool/runner.ts:228`), so shfmt ignores `format.indent_style = "tab"`. Ruff, SwiftFormat, and sqlfluff all follow it. | Pass `-i 0` when the indent style is `tab`. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/bash/manifest.toml:263-283` (`wrappers`, `embeds`) | Both checks report `node -e` and `node <<` (`INLINE_NODE` and `RUNTIME_EMBEDS`, `packages/cli/src/config/checks/language/bash.ts:116,129-138`). So one line gives two findings in two checks. | Remove inline Node from `wrappers`. `embeds` keeps it and adds `node -p`. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/bash/manifest.toml:140-149` (`contract`) | FINDINGS row 81 covers the header. The check also requires 3 more things. Every executable must define exactly one `main` and end with `main "$@"`. Every top-level assignment must be `readonly`. Directory constants must use one `CDPATH= cd -- ... && pwd -P \|\|` form (`contract.ts:95,111-114`, `bash.ts:93,119`). A 5-line script with no functions fails 3 rules. | Require `main` only in scripts that define functions. Drop the `readonly` and directory-constant rules, or turn them on with a setting. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/bash/ast-grep/branches.yml:5-10`, `nesting.yml:5-15`, `assignments.yml:4-9`, `manifest.toml:259-260` | `for ((i = 0; ...))` parses as `c_style_for_statement`, which neither rule lists. A function nested for, if, for, if was reported with 1 nested level and 2 branches. The loop's `i = 0` counts as an assignment. The summary says "reassignments", but the rule counts every plain assignment that is not `local`, `declare`, `readonly`, or `export`. | Add `c_style_for_statement` to both rules. Skip assignments inside its header. Change the summary to "assignments". |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/bash/manifest.toml:162-172`, `packages/cli/kits/language/swift/manifest.toml:172-182` (`duplicate-functions`) | Two engines find identical function bodies. They use three limits (`limits.duplicate_lines`, `limits.bash.duplicate_lines`, and `limits.swift.duplicate_lines`) and two code constants. The duplication kit's jscpd also reads Swift and shell files. Python has no such check. | Keep one engine that works for every language in the structure kit, or rely on jscpd. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/sql/manifest.toml:59-67`, `packages/cli/src/config/checks/language/sql.ts:5` | `POSTGRES_DIALECTS` includes `ansi`, and `tools.sqlfluff.dialect` defaults to `ansi`. Only the postgres kit sets a dialect. So a MySQL, SQLite, or SQL Server project gets its files parsed by the Postgres parser at `recommended`. | Parse only when the dialect is `postgres`. Treat `ansi` as "not known". |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/sql/manifest.toml:111-119`, `packages/cli/src/checks/language/sql.ts:200-210` (`sql/functions`) | The engine does not check the dialect. A parse failure throws, so at `all` any non-Postgres SQL file makes the check error. The title says "function size", but the check reports functions that are too small and lists of too many parameters. | Skip unless the dialect is `postgres`. Rename the check to `trivial-functions`, as in python, swift, and bash, and report parameters under their own rule name. |

The SQL engine reads `file_lines`, `trivial_statements`, and `function_parameters`. `limits.function_lines` lists `sql`, and `limits.cyclomatic_complexity` lists `bash`, but no code reads either for those languages. | Delete `limits.sql.function_lines`. Remove `sql` and `bash` from those `languages` lists. |

finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/sql/manifest.toml:5,76` | The `why` of `block-comments` says the spelling checks read only line comments. typos reads the whole file, block comments included. Only Vale skips block comments, because gspot maps SQL to Vale's Lua format (`packages/cli/src/config/generation/generation.ts:103-105`). The kit description claims "names checked by category", but no SQL check does that. The naming kit does. | Name Vale as the reason, or map SQL to a format in which Vale reads both comment styles and delete the check. Remove the naming claim from the description. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/sql/manifest.toml:24-38`, `packages/cli/kits/language/python/manifest.toml:46-47` (`[[tool.replace]]`) | sqlfluff also reads `[tool.sqlfluff]` in `pyproject.toml`, and basedpyright reads `[tool.basedpyright]` and `[tool.pyright]`.
